DependencyOptions packages-v3/plugin/src/types.ts:275

Used when creating a Dependency, see that.

type DependencyOptions = {
  readonly specifier: DependencySpecifier;

The specifier used to resolve the dependency.

  readonly specifierType?: SpecifierType | null;

How the specifier should be interpreted.

  • esm: An ES module specifier. It is parsed as a URL, but bare specifiers are treated as node_modules.
  • commonjs: A CommonJS specifier. It is not parsed as a URL.
  • url: A URL that works as in a browser. Bare specifiers are treated as relative URLs.
  • custom: A custom specifier. Must be handled by a custom resolver plugin.

Default value: 'esm'

  readonly priority?: DependencyPriority | null;

When the dependency should be loaded.

  • sync: The dependency should be resolvable synchronously. The resolved asset will be placed in the same bundle as the parent, or another bundle that's already on the page.
  • parallel: The dependency should be placed in a separate bundle that's loaded in parallel with the current bundle.
  • lazy: The dependency should be placed in a separate bundle that's loaded later.

Default value: 'sync'

  readonly bundleBehavior?: BundleBehavior | 'none' | null;

Controls the behavior of the bundle the resolved asset is placed into. Use in combination with priority to determine when the bundle is loaded.

  • inline: The resolved asset will be placed into a new inline bundle. Inline bundles are not written to a separate file, but embedded into the parent bundle.
  • isolated: The resolved asset will be isolated from its parents in a separate bundle. Shared assets will be duplicated.
  readonly importType?: ImportType | null;

How the resolved asset is used by the importing asset.

Default value: 'javascript'

  readonly needsStableName?: boolean | null;

When the dependency is a bundle entry (priority is "parallel" or "lazy"), this controls the naming of that bundle. needsStableName indicates that the name should be stable over time, even when the content of the bundle changes. This is useful for entries that a user would manually enter the URL for, as well as for things like service workers or RSS feeds, where the URL must remain consistent over time.

  readonly isOptional?: boolean | null;

Whether the dependency is optional. If the dependency cannot be resolved, this will not fail the build.

  readonly isEntry?: boolean | null;

Whether the dependency is an entry.

  readonly sideEffects?: boolean | null;

Whether the dependency has side effects.

  readonly loc?: {
    readonly filePath?: string | null;
    readonly start: Location;
    readonly end: Location;
  } | null;

The location within the source file where the dependency was found. filePath may be an absolute path or a URL, and defaults to the asset's.

  readonly target?: Target | null;

The target to resolve the dependency in. Must be a Target obtained from Parcel, e.g. from an asset or dependency. Defaults to the asset's target.

  readonly packageConditions?: Array<PackageConditionName> | null;

A list of package.json "exports" and "imports" conditions to use when resolving the dependency.

  readonly pipeline?: string | null;

The pipeline defined in .parcelrc that the dependency should be processed with.

  readonly resolveFrom?: string | null;

The absolute file path or URL where the dependency should be resolved from. By default, this is the source file where the dependency was specified.

  readonly range?: SemverRange | null;

The semver version range expected for the dependency.

}

Asset packages-v3/plugin/src/types.ts:460

An asset represents a file or part of a file. It may represent any data type, including source code, binary data, etc. Assets may exist in the file system or may be virtual.

Assets passed to namers, optimizers and reporters are read-only, and can only be accessed during the plugin call they were passed to.

interface Asset {
  readonly url: string;

The URL of the asset, including its query. Files on disk use file: URLs.

  readonly filePath: FilePath;

The file path of the asset.

  readonly type: string;

The asset's type. This initially corresponds to the source file extension, but it may be changed during transformation.

  readonly target: Target;

The target of the asset.

  readonly isSource: boolean;

Whether this asset is part of the project, and not an external dependency (e.g. in node_modules). This indicates that transformation using the project's configuration should be applied.

  readonly bundleBehavior: BundleBehavior | undefined;

Controls which bundle the asset is placed into.

  • inline: The asset will be placed into a new inline bundle. Inline bundles are not written to a separate file, but embedded into the parent bundle.
  • isolated: The asset will be isolated from its parents in a separate bundle. Shared assets will be duplicated.
  readonly sideEffects: boolean;

Whether this asset can be omitted if none of its exports are being used. This is initially set by the resolver, but can be overridden by transformers.

  readonly uniqueKey: string | undefined;

A key that identifies the asset, set by a transformer.

  readonly pipeline: string | undefined;

The pipeline defined in .parcelrc that the asset should be processed with.

  getCode(): string;

Returns the asset contents as a string.

  getBuffer(): Uint8Array;

Returns the asset contents as bytes.

  getMap(): SourceMapJSON | null;

Returns a copy of the source map for the asset, if available.

  getDependencies(): Array<Dependency>;

Returns a snapshot of the asset's dependencies.

}

type ResolveOptions = {
  readonly specifierType?: SpecifierType;

How the specifier should be interpreted.

  • esm: An ES module specifier. It is parsed as a URL, but bare specifiers are treated as node_modules.
  • commonjs: A CommonJS specifier. It is not parsed as a URL.
  • url: A URL that works as in a browser. Bare specifiers are treated as relative URLs.
  • custom: A specifier only a resolver plugin knows how to interpret.

Default value: 'esm'

  readonly importType?: ImportType;

How the resolved file is used, as for a dependency. A file resolved as javascript must have a transformer that turns it into JavaScript, or resolving it fails. Use url to resolve any file, e.g. to read it yourself.

Default value: 'javascript'

  readonly packageConditions?: Array<PackageConditionName>;

A list of conditions to use when resolving package.json "exports" and "imports".

ResolveFn packages-v3/plugin/src/types.ts:749

Resolves specifier from the file from with the resolvers configured in .parcelrc, exactly as a dependency of the asset would be. Returns null when no resolver resolves it. Rejects with a Diagnostic carrying the resolvers' diagnostics when one fails, which reports them unchanged if thrown. Every file the resolvers read invalidates the asset.
